history.dynasty: Maratha (attributed; claimed rule of Azam Khan)
history.period: 18th century (traditional account; exact founding date unverified)
history.summary: The Bhadrakali Temple sits inside Bhadra Fort near Lal Darwaza in Ahmedabad's walled old city. Local accounts say it was built by the Marathas during the rule of Azam Khan, though no reliable source gives a precise construction date (Azam Khan was historically a Mughal governor of Gujarat in the 17th century, so the chronology needs verification). Goddess Bhadrakali, a fierce form of Durga, is venerated as the Nagar Devi (city goddess) of Ahmedabad; devotees worship her for prosperity, wealth, and protection. The temple sees its largest crowds during Navratri, when it is elaborately decorated.

name: Bhadrakali Temple
town_description: Ahmedabad is Gujarat's largest city and its former capital, founded in 1411 by Sultan Ahmed Shah I on the banks of the Sabarmati river. Its walled old city became India's first UNESCO World Heritage City in 2017, known for carved wooden havelis, pols, stepwells, and Sultanate-era monuments. Today it is a major industrial and commercial hub, famous for its food culture, the Sabarmati Ashram, and as the gateway to Gujarat.

travel.airport: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport, ~10-11 km (verify)
travel.road: Near Lal Darwaza in the old city; reachable by city bus, auto-rickshaw, and taxi. Bhadra Fort itself is open roughly 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri (Sep/Oct) draws the biggest crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM - 10:30 PM daily (verify); aarti reported at ~8:30 AM and ~9:00 PM (verify). Photography may be restricted inside.
